rows.rationale: Important baseline: the legal concept of driver is not simply replaced by an 'operator'; some regimes preserve, redistribute or deem performance of driver duties.

extra.Core function: Drives the vehicle and bears traffic-rule duties unless an ADS is deemed to satisfy the driver requirement under Article 34 bis.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: 1968 Convention on Road Traffic, as amended by Article 34 bis
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: vodič under Act No. 8/2009 Coll.; selected automated-driving duties
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: not the core new draft role
extra.Functional equivalence: Strong for human-driver concept; limited once ADS performs the driving task
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Baseline driver concept; do not use 'operator' as automatic substitute.

rows.regime_label: ADS as functional substitute for driver requirement
rows.rationale: Critical ontology distinction: a technical system may perform the driving task without becoming the person legally responsible for service operation, compliance or supervision.
rows.term: Automated driving system satisfying Article 34 bis conditions

extra.Core function: Performs dynamic driving in a manner that can satisfy the Convention's driver requirement when conforming to applicable technical rules or domestic legislation.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: 1968 Convention on Road Traffic, Article 34 bis
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: No general autonomous legal person; ADS is treated as vehicle/system functionality
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: ADS remains distinct from operator and supervision roles
extra.Functional equivalence: Conceptual only; do not equate system with legal operator
extra.Slovak drafting implication: ADS can perform DDT without becoming the legal operator.

rows.rationale: Must remain distinct from remote driving. Advice/assistance does not automatically mean takeover of lateral and longitudinal control.

extra.Core function: Provides information or support to the ADS without necessarily assuming continuous DDT control.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: UNECE ADS Guidance and Interpretation work on remote intervention / interaction
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: No settled general statutory category in current Slovak law
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Closest candidates: control-centre and supervision functions; exact mapping unresolved
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Keep remote assistance distinct from remote driving.

rows.rationale: Do not conflate with vehicle owner, ADS manufacturer/provider or remote human supervisor.

extra.Core function: Organises or operates the transport service in which fully automated vehicles are deployed.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/1426, as amended
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: No complete general current-law equivalent for commercial FAV operation
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Closest: prevádzkovateľ plne automatizovaného vozidla / licence-holder architecture
extra.Functional equivalence: Partial to strong at service-operator level, subject to exact statutory text
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Potential comparator for Slovak licensed FAV operator.

rows.rationale: Ontology should model this primarily as a function or organisational capability, not automatically as one named natural person.

extra.Core function: Supports fleet/vehicle operation remotely within the approved system architecture, including defined interaction with vehicles and operational management.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: Regulation (EU) 2022/1426 and JRC interpretation addendum on Safety Management System and Remote Management
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: No general fully developed current-law equivalent
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Closest: riadiace centrum / control-centre functions
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Model as function/capability, not automatically as a person.

rows.regime_label: Authorised self-driving entity / ADS legal-responsibility entity
rows.rationale: High-value comparison for Slovak drafting: UK separates the entity responsible for the authorised self-driving feature from individual users and service-operation roles.

extra.Core function: Legally responsible for ensuring an authorised automated vehicle continues to meet self-driving requirements and other statutory obligations.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: Automated Vehicles Act 2024
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: No direct current-law equivalent
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Closest: licensed FAV operator, but functions are not necessarily identical
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Separate ADS safety-responsibility entity from service operator.

rows.regime_label: User with limited in-vehicle legal duties during self-driving
rows.rationale: Useful to prevent collapsing 'driver', 'user' and 'operator' into one category.

extra.Core function: Occupies the vehicle and retains specified non-driving legal duties while not responsible for the manner of driving during authorised self-driving.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: Automated Vehicles Act 2024
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: Partly comparable to driver / person required to take over under selected automated-driving rules
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Draft role allocation should be checked; not equivalent to supervision operator
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Do not conflate in-vehicle user with supervision operator.

rows.rationale: Potential model for commercial driverless operation in Slovakia where no human user-in-charge is present.

extra.Core function: Undertakes responsibilities that cannot be allocated to an in-vehicle user where the vehicle operates without a user-in-charge.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: Automated Vehicles Act 2024
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: No current-law equivalent
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Closest: licensed operator of fully automated vehicle/service
extra.Functional equivalence: Moderate to strong at organisational level
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Strong model for driverless commercial operation entity.

rows.rationale: A key warning against translating Technische Aufsicht simply as remote driver: German law deliberately separates supervision/authorisation from continuous vehicle control.

extra.Core function: Performs legally defined remote technical-supervision functions, including assessment and enabling/authorising specified manoeuvres or measures when the automated vehicle requests support.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: German Road Traffic Act (StVG), §§ 1d–1f; Autonomous Vehicles Approval and Operation Ordinance (AFGBV)
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: No settled current-law general equivalent
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Closest: operátor dohľadu / technický dohľad, but scope must be compared provision-by-provision
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Closest supervision comparator; not remote driver.

rows.rationale: France structures responsibility around the transport system/service, not only around the individual vehicle.
rows.term: Exploitant du système de transport routier automatisé

extra.Core function: Operates the automated road transport system under the French service-level safety and commissioning framework.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: Ordonnance n° 2021-443 and Décret n° 2021-873
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: No complete current-law equivalent
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Closest: licensed operator / service operator architecture
extra.Functional equivalence: Partial to strong at service-system level
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Service/system operator model; distinct from remote human role.

rows.rationale: French law is useful because it expressly links remote intervention to personal legal responsibility; this is a distinct design choice from pure technical supervision.
rows.term: Personne habilitée à intervenir à distance

extra.Core function: Performs legally authorised remote intervention within the conditions laid down for the automated road transport system.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: Ordonnance n° 2021-443; Code des transports / implementing decree
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: No explicit general current-law equivalent
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Closest: operátor dohľadu or a future remote-intervention role, depending on draft wording
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Good comparator for explicit remote-intervention powers.

rows.rationale: Useful counter-example: Croatia explicitly names an in-vehicle operator separately from a remote intervention operator.

extra.Core function: Human role located in the vehicle under the Croatian statutory architecture for automated vehicle operation.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: Croatia Road Traffic Safety Act amendments, NN 145/2024
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: No dedicated equivalent in current Slovak general framework
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Could overlap with a readiness/supervision person depending on final draft design
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Useful in-vehicle operator comparator; ADS retains DDT.

rows.rationale: Strong comparative candidate for Slovak legislative drafting because Croatia separates remote intervention from in-vehicle operation.

extra.Core function: Performs remote intervention functions for a fully automated vehicle under Croatian law.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: Croatia Road Traffic Safety Act amendments, NN 145/2024
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: No explicit general current-law equivalent
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Closest: operátor dohľadu, but remote-intervention powers need separate analysis
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Strong comparator if Slovak role intervenes but ADS remains DDT performer.

rows.rationale: Status flag is essential: as of 26 August 2026 this is not effective law and should never be returned as a current Slovak legal role without qualification.
rows.term: Prevádzkovateľ plne automatizovaného vozidla – proposed licence-holder role
rows.verification: Draft text checked; not in force

extra.Core function: Would hold the licence and carry central organisational and operational obligations for fully automated vehicle operation.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: Government bill, parliamentary print 1329
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: No general current-law commercial-operation equivalent; §49 Act 106/2018 is test-operation permit architecture
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Exact draft role
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Draft reference point for commercial-operation responsibility.

rows.rationale: Key research issue: determine whether the draft function is closer to German Technische Aufsicht, French authorised remote intervener, Croatian remote intervention operator, or an EU remote-management function. It may improperly combine several models.
rows.verification: Draft text checked; not in force

extra.Core function: Would perform supervision functions assigned by the proposed Slovak framework within the control-centre/operator structure.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: Government bill, parliamentary print 1329
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: No settled general equivalent in current law
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Exact draft role
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Core Slovak issue: define boundary between supervision, intervention and remote driving.

rows.rationale: Critical distinction for Level 3: fallback-ready user is not a remote supervisor and is not the service operator.
rows.verification: Primary technical standard checked via ROAT

extra.Core function: Remains receptive to a request to intervene and performs the DDT fallback when the Level 3 ADS can no longer continue.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: SAE J3016_202104 – Taxonomy and Definitions for Terms Related to Driving Automation Systems for On-Road Motor Vehicles
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: Closest to a driver/person subject to takeover duties in automated-driving rules; no general standalone statutory category
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Should remain distinct from operátor dohľadu; check whether draft allocates any takeover role to an in-vehicle user
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Keep Level 3 fallback user outside remote-supervision category.

rows.rationale: This is the cleanest comparator for testing whether Slovak supervision powers cross the line into actual remote driving.
rows.verification: Primary technical standard checked via ROAT

extra.Core function: Performs part or all of the dynamic driving task from outside the conventional in-vehicle driving position.
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: No explicit general remote-driver category in current Slovak road-traffic framework
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: No clearly separate remote-driver role; must not be presumed identical to operátor dohľadu
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Explicit separate remote-driver role is needed if direct DDT is ever intended.

rows.rationale: Useful reminder that strategic trip management, DDT performance and remote supervision are separate functions.
rows.verification: Primary technical standard checked via ROAT

extra.Core function: Dispatches an ADS-operated vehicle and performs strategic trip functions without performing the DDT.
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: No standalone statutory equivalent
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Possible control-centre dispatch function, but not necessarily a named legal role
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Separate dispatch/strategic functions from safety supervision.

rows.rationale: Testing roles should be kept separate from deployment roles; otherwise prototype safeguards can be mistaken for permanent operational governance.
rows.verification: Primary SAE source checked; dedicated ROAT J3018 record missing

extra.Core function: Specially trained person who supervises prototype ADS performance and is prepared to respond to unexpected ADS or vehicle behaviour.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: SAE J3018_202012 – Safety-Relevant Guidance for On-Road Testing of Prototype ADS-Operated Vehicles
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: Closest functional analogue is a test-operation safety driver/person able to intervene under the Slovak test-permit regime
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Not a core commercial-operation role in draft 1329
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Prototype-testing safeguard; do not transplant automatically into deployment.

rows.rationale: This role becomes an ordinary test driver once it actually assumes the complete DDT.
rows.verification: Primary SAE source checked; dedicated ROAT J3018 record missing

extra.Core function: Monitors prototype ADS and can safely take over through the vehicle’s in-vehicle braking, acceleration, steering and gear-selection controls.
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: Strong functional comparator for a human safety driver during Slovak public-road testing
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: No equivalent needed for genuinely driverless deployment unless retained as a special safeguard
extra.Functional equivalence: Strong in testing; weak in deployment
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Strong comparator for Slovak safety driver in public-road testing.

rows.rationale: High-value boundary case: remote fallback test driving is materially different from remote assistance and supervision.
rows.verification: Primary SAE source checked; guidance expressly limited

extra.Actor type: Natural person / trained remote test role
extra.Core function: Remote variant of the fallback test-driver concept, intended to respond to ADS testing situations from outside the vehicle.
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: No explicit current Slovak category
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Should not be collapsed into operátor dohľadu without explicit authority for remote DDT
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Do not hide remote DDT inside generic supervision terminology.

rows.regime_label: Safety driver in public-road AV testing
rows.rationale: California 2026 rules retain a distinct permitting pathway for testing with a safety driver, separate from driverless testing and deployment.
rows.term: Autonomous vehicle test driver / safety driver

extra.Core function: Provides the human driving and safety fallback required for AV testing under the drivered-testing permit category.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: California Code of Regulations, title 13, AV testing regulations; DMV 2026 framework
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: Functional analogue of the human safety driver used under a Slovak test-operation permit
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Not a necessary deployment role for fully driverless operation
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Testing-only human safeguard.

rows.rationale: Useful for separating testing authorisation from commercial/deployment operator licensing in Slovak law.
rows.term: Manufacturer / autonomous vehicle testing permit holder

extra.Core function: Holds DMV authority to test or deploy AVs subject to the applicable permit category, ODD, reporting and compliance conditions.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: California DMV Autonomous Vehicle Regulations and Permit Program
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: Closest current comparator: holder/applicant of a §49 Act No. 106/2018 test-operation permit
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Draft licensed FAV operator is closer for deployment, but not identical to California testing permit holder
extra.Functional equivalence: Strong for testing permit; partial for deployment
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Separate Slovak §49 permit holder from eventual deployment licence holder.

rows.rationale: Strong comparator for redesigning Slovak test operation as a controlled validation/trial phase rather than conflating it with deployment.
rows.term: Permit holder for trial operation with automated vehicles
rows.verification: Official regulator framework checked; dedicated ROAT primary record missing

extra.Actor type: Person or organisation holding trial permit
extra.Core function: Obtains permission for automated-vehicle trials and must demonstrate that the trial can be conducted in a traffic-safe manner subject to permit conditions.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: Swedish ordinance on trial operation with automated vehicles and TSFS 2021:4 permit process
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: Close functional analogue to holder of a Slovak §49 test-operation permit
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Distinct from draft commercial FAV operator licence
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Strong comparator for a redesigned Slovak validation/trial regime.

rows.rationale: Important comparator to UK ASDE: both separate ADS safety responsibility from ordinary vehicle ownership and human user roles.
rows.framework: Australia – proposed Automated Vehicle Safety Law framework
rows.verification: Official Australian policy framework checked; proposed law not yet in force

extra.Core function: Certified corporation responsible for the safety of an ADS over its on-road design life, including safety-management, data and in-service obligations.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: Australian NTC automated-vehicle regulatory framework; proposed Automated Vehicle Safety Law
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: No current-law equivalent
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Closest candidate is licensed FAV operator, but ADSE is specifically ADS-lifecycle-safety oriented and may be closer to an ADS provider/manufacturer responsibility holder
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Potential missing Slovak role: ADS lifecycle safety entity separate from service operator.

rows.rationale: Japan is valuable because it separates the permission-holding implementer from the natural-person supervisor responsible for remote monitoring and accident response.
rows.framework: Japan – Road Traffic Act SAO framework
rows.verification: Official National Police Agency framework checked; dedicated ROAT primary record missing

extra.Core function: Holds permission for specified automated operation, complies with the approved SAO plan, educates staff and establishes the organisational measures required by the Road Traffic Act.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: Japan Road Traffic Act, as amended by Act No. 32 of 2022 – SAO permission framework
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: No general current-law equivalent for driverless commercial operation
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Strong candidate comparator for licensed FAV operator / licence-holder architecture
extra.Functional equivalence: Partial to strong at permission-holder level
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Clean model for separating permission-holder entity from supervisor.

rows.rationale: A particularly clean comparator if Slovak law intends supervision without continuous remote DDT control.
rows.framework: Japan – Road Traffic Act SAO framework
rows.verification: Official National Police Agency framework checked; dedicated ROAT primary record missing

extra.Core function: Monitors the state of remote monitoring equipment and performs legally assigned accident-response and reporting measures for SAO.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: Japan Road Traffic Act SAO permission framework
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: No explicit current-law equivalent
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Potentially close to operátor dohľadu, especially for remote monitoring and incident response
extra.Functional equivalence: Partial to strong, subject to exact Slovak powers
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Strong comparator for supervision without direct remote driving.

rows.rationale: Ontario explicitly keeps the participant responsible at all times even when an assistant provides remote or in-vehicle oversight.
rows.term: ACMV Pilot Program participant / approval package holder
rows.verification: Official Ontario programme conditions checked; dedicated current primary regulation record missing

extra.Core function: Holds programme approval, develops a graduated testing framework, ensures compliance and remains responsible for the automated commercial motor vehicle throughout the pilot.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: Ontario Automated Commercial Motor Vehicle Pilot Program Conditions / applicable HTA pilot regulation
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: Closest current comparator is a test-operation permit holder under §49 Act No. 106/2018
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Not equivalent to permanent licensed FAV operator because Ontario role is pilot-specific
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Participant remains responsible even where human oversight is delegated.

rows.rationale: High-value drafting model because the legal boundary is explicit: oversight may include safe-stop/manoeuvring/advice, but not remote control for regular driving tasks.
rows.verification: Official Ontario programme conditions checked; dedicated primary regulation record missing

extra.Core function: Provides oversight from inside the vehicle or elsewhere in Ontario; may initiate a safe stop, manoeuvre to clear the way or advise decision-making, but must not remotely control regular driving tasks.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: Ontario Automated Commercial Motor Vehicle Pilot Program Conditions
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: No explicit current-law equivalent
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Very close comparator for operátor dohľadu if Slovak law intends oversight, advice and exceptional safe-state action without ordinary remote driving
extra.Functional equivalence: Potentially strong; powers must be compared
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Excellent comparator for defining operátor dohľadu without remote-driving creep.

rows.regime_label: Vehicle owner as statutory responsibility holder
rows.rationale: Croatia is a useful warning against conflating owner, service operator and remote human roles: the owner carries specific offence and data duties even though intervention roles are separately defined.

extra.Core function: Bears statutory responsibility for traffic offences committed by the fully automated vehicle subject to exceptions, and has data-preservation/disclosure duties.
extra.Primary legal / technical source: Croatia Road Traffic Safety Act amendments, NN 145/2024, Articles 281.d–281.e
extra.Slovak current-law equivalent: Vehicle owner/holder concepts exist, but Slovak AV law does not currently use ownership as a complete substitute for driver/operator responsibility
extra.Slovak draft 1329 equivalent: Draft operator/licence-holder should remain distinct from vehicle owner unless the law expressly combines them
extra.Functional equivalence: Partial – ownership is a separate legal axis
extra.Slovak drafting implication: Keep owner/holder liability axis separate from operator and supervisor roles.
